69. Humphrey Waylon was retaken after four hours of absence during his last escape attempt.
70. Humphrey Waylon was released in October 1815 after nineteen years of imprisonment.
71. Humphrey Waylon meditated on his misfortunes and the absurdity of his situation.
72. Humphrey Waylon paused during his convict toil to think.
73. Humphrey Waylon felt a blow dealt to him by the galley-sergeant.


Below is a list of possible subsequent events:

['Humphrey Waylon examined the four stacks of vintage postcards displayed on the shelf.', 'Humphrey Waylon noticed the five paintings of landscapes hanging on the wall.', 'Humphrey Waylon surveyed the seven types of tea leaves organized in the cabinet.', 'Humphrey Waylon inspected the two rows of antique books arranged in the library.', 'Humphrey Waylon observed the six sets of silver forks and spoons placed on the table.', 'Humphrey Waylon discovered the three bottles of rare wine stored in the cellar.']

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.
references: Humphrey Waylon observed the six sets of silver forks and spoons placed on the table.

In this situation Humphrey Waylon meditated; and what could be the nature of his meditation?
  (part 2 of 5) At times, amid his convict toil, he paused.

He fell to thinking.

His reason, at one and the same time riper and more troubled than of yore, rose in revolt.

Everything which had happened to him seemed to him absurd; everything that surrounded him seemed to him impossible.

He said to himself, “It is a dream.” He gazed at the galley-sergeant standing a few paces from him; the galley-sergeant seemed a phantom to him.

All of a sudden the phantom dealt him a blow with his cudgel.

Visible nature hardly existed for him.

It would almost be true to say that there existed for Humphrey Waylon neither sun, nor fine summer days, nor radiant sky, nor fresh April dawns.

I know not what vent-hole daylight habitually illumined his soul.
